Tapir: Whole brown tapir with elongated flexible snout, rounded pale-edged ears and four separate complete feet. Short tail stays attached. Far upper-leg emergence remains partly concealed; source candidate only.
Wild Boar: Whole brown bristled boar, raised mane, long snout and visible curved tusk, four separated hooved lower limbs and attached tufted tail. Far shoulder origin partially hidden by torso; fringe ownership must be reviewed.
Peccary: Stocky bristled dark subject with pale shoulder collar and four separated hooves; no long boar tail. Two conspicuous downward tusks require species-identity review, not automatic acceptance.
Coati: Long narrow muzzle and upright banded bushy tail; four separated feet with claws. Tail/root continuity visible; far ear mostly hidden and far upper limb concealed. No invented joint claim.
Porcupine: Dense black-and-cream long quills over rounded body with four exposed clawed feet. Near ear visible; far ear concealed by quills. Quill and tail-tip ownership require full-size scoring.
Impala: Slender tan body, white belly, black tail/rump marks, long ridged lyre horns and four separated hooves. Second ear obscured by horns/head; horns must not be misclassified as ears.
Warthog: Sparse bristled brown body, cheek warts and large curved paired tusks; upright thin tufted tail and four complete hooves. Mane strands are attached but need island scoring.
Buffalo: Heavy brown-black body, broad fused-looking horn boss and curved horns, drooping near ear, four separated hooves and tufted tail. Far ear concealed; do not invent it.
Badger: White and black facial stripes, grizzled body and strong claws on four feet. Tail appears much longer and bushier than expected for the canonical badger: identity hold for Claude, even though framing passes.
River Otter: Long brown body, pale muzzle/throat, small rounded ears and long tapering thick tail, four visible clawed feet. Limb emergence still partly hidden by body fur; webbing not independently clear.
Beaver: Broad flattened scaly paddle tail, rounded brown body, orange incisors and four distinct feet. Far ear concealed and rear webbing not plainly readable; candidate requires anatomy scoring.
Wolverine: Stocky dark body with broad pale flank bands and bushy tail, rounded ears, four strong separated clawed feet. Tail fully framed; far ear only partially visible.
Ibex: Long heavy ridged swept horns, beard, brown coat and four separate hooves; short pale-ended tail. Far ear obscured by horn/head. No claimed hidden ear landmark.
Chamois: Short hooked horns, pale face with dark eye stripe, tan coat, dark lower legs and four separate hooves. Short tail visible; both ear silhouettes mostly readable.
Fishing Cat: Dense dark spots over grey-brown body and facial stripes; thick short ringed tail and four separate feet. Some far upper limb remains obscured; spots remain distinct.
Spotted Hyena: Heavy front shoulders, sloping back, rounded ears, spotted sandy coat, dark muzzle and short bushy tail. Four complete separated feet; dark spots preserved across body.
Aardvark: Long tubular snout, large upright ears, arched brown body, long thick tapered tail and four strong clawed feet. Source shows natural rounded haunch rather than a generic long-legged frame.
Bison: Massive shoulder hump, dense shaggy front coat and beard, short horns, four complete hooves and tufted tail. Far ear concealed by mane/horn. Head-down fur ownership needs scoring.
Prairie Dog: Small sandy rodent with rounded head, small ears, short dark-tipped tail and four visible clawed feet. Near/far limb roots remain partly obscured by rounded torso.
Wild Horse: Dun body, upright dark mane, pale muzzle, dark lower legs and long dark tail; four complete hooves. Ear tips and mane remain within frame; near/far upper legs partly overlap naturally.
Goat: Brown-white coat, beard, paired swept horns, two ears, short raised tail and four hooves. Fine beard and tail fringes need island/ownership review.
Cat: Brown tabby with visible dark striping, pale muzzle/chest, long ringed tail and four complete paws. Both ears visible; patterned face and body remain distinct.
Dog: Brown-white medium dog, upright ears, white chest and feet, curled bushy tail and four separated paws. Fur fringes attached; no anatomical landmarks inferred from coat alone.
Llama: Long neck, long inward-curved ears, shaggy brown-white coat and four separate feet with short tail. Lower foot anatomy and upper-leg visibility need independent review.
